# Phase 999.12: Editor UX Enhancements - Context

**Gathered:** 2026-04-07
**Status:** Ready for planning
**Mode:** Auto-generated (autonomous execution — spec is enumerated requirement list)

<domain>
## Phase Boundary

Pro-grade UX features for the existing video editor (built in 999.10,
stabilized in 999.11). Quality-of-life improvements that bring the
editor closer to VEED/CapCut/Descript-tier interaction polish — without
introducing new architectural primitives.

In scope: timeline interactions, selection model, snapping, nudging,
overlay guides, export progress, validation, persistence of user prefs,
per-track controls, subtitle style presets.

Out of scope: anything that touches narration generation, script gen,
ffmpeg pipeline, Remotion compositions beyond the SafeZone overlay, or
the Kie credit system.

</domain>

<decisions>
## Implementation Decisions

### Selection model
- **D-01:** Multi-select via shift-click and ctrl/cmd-click on timeline
  blocks (scenes, subtitles, audio items). Selection is a `Set<string>`
  in the Zustand store, replacing the existing `selectedSceneId`/etc.
  scalars where applicable. Backwards compatible: single selection still
  exposes `selectedSceneId` getter from the set's first element to avoid
  rewriting every consumer in PropertiesPanel.
- **D-02:** Bulk operations (delete, duplicate, nudge) apply to all
  selected items via existing per-item methods iterated in a single
  zustand `set` call so undo/redo treats it as one history entry.
- **D-03:** Click on empty timeline area (the track background, not a
  block) deselects everything. Implementation: pointerdown handler on
  TimelineTrack with `e.target === e.currentTarget` check.

### Snapping
- **D-04:** Snap-to-playhead and snap-to-block-edges during drag and
  trim. Snap threshold: 6px in screen space (converted to frames via
  current zoom). Snap targets: playhead frame, every other block's
  start/end frame, scene boundaries.
- **D-05:** Snap is on by default; hold Alt to disable temporarily
  (industry standard from Premiere/Resolve). Toggle in Toolbar for
  permanent off.

### Nudging
- **D-06:** Arrow keys nudge selected subtitle/audio block by 1 frame.
  Shift+Arrow nudges by 10 frames. Cmd/Ctrl+Arrow nudges by 1 second
  (currentFps frames). Only active when focus is on the timeline area
  (not in a text input).
- **D-07:** Nudge respects multi-select — all selected items shift by
  the same delta as one undo entry.

### Auto-pause on subtitle drag
- **D-08:** When user starts dragging a subtitle in the preview overlay
  AND the player is currently playing, auto-pause. Resume is manual.
  Implementation: pointerdown handler on subtitle overlay calls
  `playerRef.current?.pause()`.

### Per-clip volume
- **D-09:** Add `volume: number` (0..1, default 1) to `EditorAudioItem`
  type. Properties panel shows a Radix Slider when an audio block is
  selected. Remotion `<Audio>` component receives `volume={item.volume}`.
- **D-10:** No per-scene clip volume slider — scenes have no audio
  source separate from the audio track in our current model. Defer.

### Safe-zone guides overlay
- **D-11:** Overlay rendered on top of `RemotionPreview` (not inside the
  Remotion composition — avoids polluting the export render). Two
  configurable zones based on platform: TikTok (top 220px, bottom 240px,
  right 80px) and Instagram Reels (top 130px, bottom 175px, right 70px),
  scaled to the 9:16 preview viewport. Toggle button in Toolbar with a
  dropdown to pick platform. State persists in `localStorage` per user.
- **D-12:** Render as semi-transparent red zones (rgba 239 68 68 / 0.18)
  with dashed border. Pointer-events: none so it never blocks clicks.

### Zoom-to-fit
- **D-13:** New Toolbar button "Fit" that resets the timeline horizontal
  zoom to whatever level fits the entire `totalDuration()` into the
  current viewport width. Computation lives in `use-timeline-zoom.ts`.
  Keyboard shortcut: `Shift+Z`.

### Export progress
- **D-14:** Replace fire-and-forget POST `/reels/{id}/export-remotion`
  with a polling pattern: backend writes `step_state.export.progress`
  (0-100) and `step_state.export.status` ("queued" | "rendering" |
  "done" | "error"). Frontend shows a modal with a progress bar that
  polls `useStepState` every 1.5s while status !== "done"|"error".
- **D-15:** On completion, modal shows "Download" button and the modal
  stays open until user closes (so they can re-download). On error,
  shows the backend error message verbatim.

### Pre-export validation
- **D-16:** Before triggering export, run a synchronous client-side
  validator over the editor state. Checks (lib/editor/validate.ts):
  - No gaps between scenes (a scene's start must equal previous scene's
    end — they're contiguous in the current model so this is just an
    invariant check, log only if violated)
  - No subtitle overlaps that span >50% of each other's duration (use
    existing `subsOverlapping` from lib/editor)
  - No audio items extending beyond `totalDuration()`
  - At least 1 scene exists
  - All scenes have either `clipUrl` or `imgUrl`
- **D-17:** Validation results shown in a modal listing each issue with
  severity (warning/error). Errors block export; warnings show a
  "Export anyway" button.

### Resizable timeline panel
- **D-18:** The horizontal split between the preview/properties panel
  (top) and the timeline (bottom) is draggable. Use a vertical resize
  handle. Min timeline height: 180px. Max: 60% of viewport. Persisted
  in localStorage.

### Per-track mute/solo
- **D-19:** Each timeline track (Video, Audio, Legendas) gets a small
  M (mute) and S (solo) toggle in its track header. Mute hides the
  track from the Remotion preview; solo mutes all other tracks.
- **D-20:** Implementation: add `mutedTracks: Set<TrackKind>` and
  `soloedTracks: Set<TrackKind>` to the editor store. RemotionPreview
  consumers check the relevant set when rendering.

### Subtitle style presets
- **D-21:** A "Save as preset" button in the subtitle style section of
  PropertiesPanel writes the current subtitle's style props (font,
  color, size, shadow, position) to a `subtitlePresets` array in
  localStorage. A dropdown in the same section shows saved presets and
  applies them to the selected subtitle on click.
- **D-22:** Preset model: `{ id, name, style: SubtitleStyle }`. No
  server sync — purely client-side because presets are personal taste.
  Default preset name is "Preset N" where N is the next index; user can
  rename inline.

### Claude's Discretion
- Exact Radix component to use for the resizable panel split (likely
  `react-resizable-panels` since it's already in the Next.js ecosystem)
- Animation timing for snapping feedback (none vs subtle highlight)
- Whether bulk-operation undo entries get a different label in any UI
- Test coverage strategy — unit tests for pure functions in lib/editor,
  integration tests can wait for the next test-fixing pass

</decisions>

<code_context>
## Existing Code Insights

### Reusable Assets
- `useEditorStore` (Zustand + zundo temporal middleware, 580 lines) —
  central source of truth for scenes/subtitles/audio/transitions
- `lib/editor/` barrel export with pure functions: `parseSrt`,
  `shiftSubtitles`, `shiftAudio`, `getSceneTimeRange`, `subsInRange`,
  `subsOverlapping`, `reindexScenes`, `genId`
- `use-timeline-zoom.ts` — existing zoom logic, extend for fit-to-view
- `use-autosave.ts` — debounced autosave already wired
- Radix UI primitives: Slider, Tooltip, Dialog, ScrollArea
- `cn()` utility for class merging
- `useStepState` SWR hook for backend polling (extend for export status)

### Established Patterns
- Zustand `set` callbacks wrap state mutations; zundo automatically
  captures undo entries per `set` call
- "use client" mandatory for editor components
- Tailwind 4 with `@theme` design tokens (no tailwind.config.js)
- localStorage keys prefixed with `memelab.editor.*`
- Editor scene/subtitle/audio operations all flow through the store —
  components never mutate state directly

### Integration Points
- Add new fields to `editor-types.ts`: `volume` on EditorAudioItem,
  selection set, mute/solo sets, presets array
- Extend `lib/editor/` with: `validate.ts`, `snap.ts`, `nudge.ts`
- New components: `editor/SafeZoneOverlay.tsx`, `editor/ExportModal.tsx`,
  `editor/ValidationModal.tsx`, `editor/PresetDropdown.tsx`,
  `editor/ResizableSplit.tsx`
- Backend: extend `step_state.export` schema in
  `src/api/routes/reels.py` and `src/reels_pipeline/models.py`
- Backend: `POST /reels/{id}/export-remotion` becomes async-with-progress

</code_context>

<specifics>
## Specific Ideas

- VEED.io-style snap glow: a brief 1px white border on snap target
  (optional, can defer)
- Safe zone colors and dimensions modeled after CapCut's overlay
- Validation modal styled like an inline error list (not a popup) —
  matches the existing memelab UI density
- Mute/solo toggles use single letters (M/S) like every DAW

</specifics>

<deferred>
## Deferred Ideas

- Keyboard shortcut customization (settings panel for rebinding) —
  future
- Cloud sync of subtitle presets across devices — future, requires
  user-pref storage on backend
- Per-scene volume control (no model support today) — defer until we

- Color-coded scene types — design exploration, not in this phase
- Marker/chapter system on the timeline — future

</deferred>
